headline: Great Basin Cave Tour and Railway Ticketing
reservation: Guided tours of Lehman Caves at Great Basin National Park often sell out weeks in advance and require separate reservations from park entry. Nevada Northern Railway excursions, particularly themed holiday trains, operate on specific schedules and should be booked through their official portal. While no general entry permit is required for the town, local lodging fills during the Perseid meteor shower and regional festivals.

days.title: Steam Power and Mining Heritage

stops.name: Nevada Northern Railway Museum
stops.detail: Tour the historic East Ely Yard, a preserved complex of steam locomotives and vintage rail cars.

stops.name: Ward Charcoal Ovens State Historic Park
stops.detail: Visit the six beehive-shaped stone ovens used for silver smelting in the 1870s.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; roads to the ovens are mostly well-maintained gravel.
days.note: Railway schedules vary seasonally; check official departure times.

days.title: Peaks of the Great Basin

stops.name: Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive
stops.detail: Drive to 10,000 feet for views of the only glacier in Nevada and ancient forests.

stops.name: Lehman Caves
stops.detail: Explore ornate marble caverns featuring rare shield formations on a ranger-led walk.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours round trip; steep ascent requires focused driving.
days.note: Scenic Drive upper section typically opens in June and closes with first snow.

days.title: Desert Waters and Dark Skies

stops.name: Cave Lake State Park
stops.detail: Enjoy lakeside views and limestone cliffs in this high-altitude reservoir setting.

stops.name: Great Basin Star Train
stops.detail: Join a specialized evening rail excursion for dark-sky viewing with park rangers.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total; simple paved access to state park.
days.note: Temperature drops rapidly after sunset; bring heavy layers.

intel.title: National Park Access
intel.text: Lehman Caves Visitor Center has limited parking; arrive at least 30 minutes before tour times. Overflow parking is available but requires walking uphill.

intel.title: High Desert Isolation
intel.text: Cell service is consistent in Ely but non-existent in much of Great Basin National Park. Use the visitor center Wi-Fi for final navigation checks.

intel.title: Regional Hub Strategy
intel.text: Ely is the last major fuel stop for 70+ miles in any direction on the 'Loneliest Road.' Always top off before heading toward Baker or Tonopah.

intel.title: Steam Train Operations
intel.text: Locomotives are serviced regularly; steam vs. diesel power depends on the specific daily schedule. Check the museum calendar for active steam dates.

intel.title: High Elevation Snow
intel.text: Snow can linger on the Bristlecone Trail through July. Check the NPS trail status for current conditions before attempting high-summit hikes.

plan.arrival: Rent a car at EKO or LAS; Ely is a 3-4 hour drive from major hubs. Stock up on specialty supplies in larger cities as Ely offers basic hardware and groceries.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are sufficient for town and the main National Park road; RVs should check length limits for Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive.
plan.goldenHour: Mather Overlook on the Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive provides an expansive view of the Snake Range at sunset, weather permitting.
